1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE 25% : The buyer can increase or decrease the contract quantity or contract duration up to 25 percent at the time of issue of the contract. For lumpsum-based service contracts, the buyer may increase the scope of work and contract value up to 25 percent with the consent of the service provider 2. Service & Support AVAILABILITY OF OFFICE OF SERVICE PROVIDER: An office of the Service Provider must be located in the state of Consignee. DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE TO BE SUBMITTED. 3. Any other document in support of contract execution like Third Party Inspection release note, etc. 9. DD should be made in favour of FA & CAO, East Coast Railway, Bhubaneswar.

payable at Sambalpur . After award of contract, Successful Bidder can upload scanned copy of the DD in place of PBG and has to ensure delivery of hard copy to the original DD to the Buyer within 15 days of award of contract. 10. Service & Support The Service Provider is required to have at least 20 % of the required manpower on service provider’s payroll for at least one year. Necessary documents relating to such manpower will be uploaded by the bidder for verification of the buyer. Such manpower will be part of total manpower to be provided by the Service Provider in case he gets the contract against this bid. 11. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses SPECIAL CONDITION OF CONTRACT 1) The agency should Provide 18 (Eighteen) No. of semi skilled guard to guard & pr ovide security to railway property round the clock and to ensure that outsiders, ven dors, beggars etc do not enter into the station of PNPI, JRMA, BOUH, BRSR, PU KK, BHPI, JRTB, SNGR & CHRCK other station as decided by Railway Authority and to take instructions from Sr.DSC/RPF/E.Co.Rly/SBP and any other Railway Autho rity concerned. Any theft or damage of any railway property will be the responsibilit y of the private security guards and the cost of the materials will be debited from t he bills of the private security agency. 2) The agency should provide 18 Nos of private security guards on daily basis exclu ding rest giver. No beat will be kept unmanned. 3) The agency shall preferably deploy the Ex-Servicemen below the age of 55 years for Railway Security duty. 4) The agency must have a valid license under section 4 of the Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act, 2005 (PSARA) to undertake the district in which the Railway Establ ishment, to be secured, is located should be submitted to this office. 5) The Private Security Personnel provided to the Railway should be physically fit, sm art and free from any physical disability. 6) The agency shall have a proper system of recruitment, C&A verification of their sta ff, a district uniform and proper ID cards. 7) The Private Security Guards, to be deployed, shall be imparted one week duratio n orientation course by RPF before deployed on Railway Security duty. The Guard s shall however, not be treated as having performed duty for Railways during the p eriod of training. The expenditure on remuneration etc. of these Guards during the period of training shall be done by the concerned Private Security Agency (PSA). 8) The agency/firm/tenderer will deploy semi-skilled guards. The details of deployme nt/shift wise distribution will be advised by the Railway Administration. 9) The nature of duties would generally be as follows: - Total responsibilities of guarding of PNPI, JRMA, BOUH, BRSR, PUKK, BHPI, JRTB, SNGR & CHRCK station of newly opened BLGR-KUR Section & other vital installa tions or any other complex as decided by Railway Authority of East Coast Railway, watch & ward should be undertaken on round the clock (24X7) basis including Holid ays. Protection of Railway Property will be the prime responsibility of the agency/fir m/tenderer.

10) The agency/firm/tenderer shall ensure that no unauthorized person enters into the Station premises. 11) The agency/firm/tenderer shall apprehend culprits and hand over them to local pol ice/RPF for further course of action. 12) The agency/firm/tenderer shall lodge complaints/FIR with the police authorities on behalf of railway management and shall keep close liaison with local police authorit ies for follow up action. 13) The agency/firm/tenderer shall submit necessary report to railway Administration regarding all unusual occurrences including untoward incidents occurring in the as mentioned above of Station. 14) The agency/firm/tenderer shall carryout any other task allotted by management in the interest of watch & ward duties of railway premises within the staff strength. 15) No residential accommodation will be provided by railway administration for any of the employee of the agency/firm/tenderer. The agency will provide accommodati on in a centralize manner to the security guards deployed at SBP. 16) The agency/firm/tenderer shall be solely responsible for all acts of commission/o mission of its employees. 17) The agency/firm/tenderer shall ensure that all their guards are literate, wear stan dard uniform, badges, caps, and shoes and are equipped with torches, batons and other equipments considered necessary for discharging their duties effectively. All t hese items will be provided by the agency at their own cost. The staff on duty shall be always respectful to the Railway Management/Supervisory staff of railway. They shall be courteous to all railway staff members and visitors and politely seek inform ation if any. All Guards should be at least 10th class pass. In no case a guard should be found in untidy condition, drunken or sleeping. During night duty every guard sh ould have torch, whistle and baton always in hand and should whistle all around reg ularly. In regular intervals, the uniforms, socks etc. should be washed & pressed an d keep the leather shoes polished. 18) The security personnel deployed at SBP & will report to RPF/Post/SBP. In each shi ft, the security guards deployed at different beats to be counted by security superv isor in presence of RPF officials by putting their signature in attendance register on daily basis. 19) During duty mounting and dismounting, the security supervisor should ensure prop er briefing and debriefing about duties. Further supervisor or RPF officials may ensu re proper lineup during mounting and dismounting at respective RPF/Post to mainta in discipline and inspection of turn out. 20) The agency shall provide security personnel for the prescribed period. No extra pa yment shall be made for working on Sundays and National/General Holidays. 21) Providing security for the railway assets as per the allotment of duties/areas of re sponsibilities. 22) The personnel deployed by security agency have to be well behaved, courteous with the passengers, railways employees and general public. 23) To keep the premises, free from all sorts of undesirable elements and unauthorized persons. As and when required necessary assistance may be provided to the railwa y administration by security agency. 24) Ensure intact conditions of seals and locks during patrolling duty by security guar ds. 25) In the event of any theft, pilferage, fire, disobedience, indiscipline, unauthorized/an ti-institutional activities and all other criminal activities in railway premises, securi ty personnel shall report the same to RPF Post immediately.

26) To form queues at reservation counter/booking counters or at any other places deci ded by railway administration. 27) RESPONSIBILITY IN CASE OF THEFT/PILFERAGE: Due to negligence, default and wrongful act of security guards deployed, the cost o f the materials/ items will be recovered from the agency/firm/tenderer in case of th eft, pilferage etc. Shift Timing should be as follows: 1st shift - 21.00 hrs to 05.00 hrs. 2nd shift - 05.00 hrs to 13.00 hrs 28) The guards should report at the duty beats half an hour before commencement of their duty and remain in touch with the officer in-charge assigned by the railway ad ministration. 29) Mode of Payment: (i) Muster roll should prepare by the agency on the basis of attendance register. The a ttendance register must be kept at concerned i.e RPF/Posts for periodical checking of Rly officials. (ii) PC/RPF/BLGR should submit a monthly statement by 10th of every month regardi ng payment of wages to the Security guards deployed at yours counting the man days wo rk. Further they also ensure the payment of security guards as per the terms and conditio ns of minimum wages act and contribution towards EPF & ESI. Monthly performance of se curity guards including default, absent, negligence etc should be mentioned against each. (iii) Payment will be made on actual work done (man days) basis. (iv) The tenderer should ensure the payments of the deployed manning/upkee p personnel 1st week of every month. Any delay in payment except unavoidable cir cumstances the Railway administration has a right to impose and/or act for penalty /termination of contract/cancellation of security license or any other clause that de emed fit by the competent authority i.e. Sr.DSC/RPF/SBP without prior notice. 30) Penalty: The penalty may be imposed in the following cases: - (i) Penalty for any place/location found unmanned will be imposed Rs. 1000/- per head per day + contribution of (EPF, ESI and GST). And for not wearing complete uniform durin g duty hours a fine of Rs.300.00 will be imposed. It will be deducted amount of Rs. 1000/- each per day, if the entire beat will found unmanned. If aggrieved, contractor may prefer appeal against the penalty imposed by the authority to Sr.DSC/RPF/SBP. If labours/ workers misbehave with any railway employee/passengers or representative of the Sr.DS C, then the penalty will be imposed @ 500 per case. (ii) Proportionate deductions will be made for absence of security guards from duty si milarly; penalty can also be levied by the railways for dereliction of duty, default and unde sirable act on the part of the Security guards. Penalty may be imposed, if the contractor fa ils to submit the bills in time. (i.e in between 10th to 20th of every month). Penalty may b e imposed, if the contractor fails to furnish the desired documents within the stipulated pe riod as sought for by the Rly Administration.

31. PERIOD OF AGREEMENT: The agreement will be valid for a period of 365 days i.e 01 years from the date o f commencement of the work. The railway administration reserves the right of term ination of the contract with immediate effect. If it is established that the agency has not been able to follow Central Govt./State Govt. laws or has breached any contract agreement. The railway administration also reserves the right to terminate the agre ement by giving one month notice. 32. The agency shall be solely responsible for maintenance of discipline of the person nel so deployed by it from time to time. 33. The agency shall agree and undertake to comply with all statutory provisions of th e central, state and local bodies such as EPF,ESI etc and shall be solely responsible for any non-compliance of the same wherever such rules are made applicable to th em. 34. The agency shall be solely liable for an accident/injuries caused to their personne l or to their parties arising out of and in the course of employment and that the age ncy shall comply with the procedures such as reporting to appropriate authorities, t reatment of the injured and meeting the expenses incidental thereto, payment of c ompensation etc. 35. In the event of any theft, pilferage, loss, damage or injury, if any to the propertie s of the railways or to their employees due to negligence or omission of duty comm itted by any of the personnel of the agency, the agency shall be held liable for all th e loss/damage. Whether any such loss attributed to the negligence or any such act on the part of security agency’s security personnel or not will be decided by the rail way authorities concerned after a joint enquiry is conducted by the representatives of Sr.DSC/RPF/E.Co.Rly/SBP and the agency. 36. The agency shall arrange to conduct surprise checks and generally supervise the performance and turn out of the security guards deployed at the railway site. 37. The security agency shall ensure non-involvement of security guards directly or i ndirectly in any commercial activities or employment. 38. The security agency shall provide attractive uniforms with nameplates and equip ments as decided by railways. All security personnel deployed shall keep smart, act ive and impressive appearance and shall put on the uniform in neat and tidy conditi on. 39. The successful security agency only should execute the contract work awarded and sub-contracting of work is not permitted. 40. The security agency shall also be responsible for the various taxes/levies of the S tate Govt./Central Govt. and other statutory bodies. 41. The security agency shall not deploy/engage any worker, who has not completed the age of 18 years on the date of his deployment/engagement. 42. Security agency before deploying any persons for working, shall issue an identit y card with photo to every worker/employee duly countersigned by the authorized person in this behalf or in-charge of PSA. 43. The security agency shall cover each of his workmen under the provident fund, ESI and other miscellaneous Provision Act from the very first day of his employme nt.

44. Ensure that the security guards provided should have minimum working knowledg e of English, Hindi, Oriya and should be able to write beat books, charge books etc . 45. Ensure that the security guards shall not to indulge themselves directly or indirectl y with any of the association, councils, forums, bodies of the railway consisting of staff or labour of the railways. 46. Ensure that the security guards indulging in undesirable acts shall be changed b y the contractor forthwith on receipt of advice from the railways. The decision of t he railways as to what is an ‘undesirable act’ will not be open to question. 47. The security personnel shall be deployed for a maximum of 08 hours duty at once . 48. he security agency shall provide substitute guards immediately in case of absence T of any guard. 49. Security personnel so deployed should have adequate training in fire fighting. 50. The security agency shall provide required stationary such as uniform, torch lig ht, whistle, baton cane etc. Registers and beat book may also issue to note the de tails of the assets he has taken charge. 51. RPF Officer and staff will conduct surprise visit/checks from time to time to mon itor the duties of security guards deployed at E.Co.Rly. 52. The agency shall abide with terms and conditions of PSARA-2005 made there un der. 53. Persons suffering from contagious or infectious diseases shall not be employed or permitted to work in the railways premises. 54. ATTENDANCE REGISTER: Attendance of the guards will be maintained daily by PC/RPF/BLGR. 55. Wages (a)The contractor shall pay basic monthly wages plus statuary charges (EPF/ESI) to a ll Security guards as per the minimum wages rate fixed by Central Govt. The contractor shall provide full information in respect of the wages etc paid by him to his employees so deploy ed in conformity with the provisions of the contract labour (Regulation and Abolition ) Act, 1970 and rules, made there under. (b)The contractor shall furnish details of disbursement of salary to the PC/RPF/SBP wi thin 5 days from the date of disbursement respectively. The security Agency shall maintain attendance registers, individual’s ledger/wage book, wage slip, publication s of scale of wages and terms of employment. (c)The Contractor shall be responsible for fulfilling all his obligations towards the sec urity guards deployed under the Minimum Wages Act., EPF Act, ESI Act and Bonus A ct, be responsible for the deposit of employee’s and principle employer’s share of st atutory contributions with the ESI/EPF authorities at his own level and maintenance of such record as per rules. The agency will furnish the proof of deposit of such cont ributions to the appropriate authority i.e. Sr.DSC/RPF/SBP along with wage bill for th e next month. He will also arrange to open such EPF/ESI accounts etc. of all the Sec

urity Guards deployed by the Agency. In case of failure on the part of contractor to deposit EPF/ESI etc. with the concerned authorities within the stipulated period the contractor shall be liable to pay penalty so imposed by the authority. 56. The Contractor shall confirm to the provisions of various Central/State Act(s) or t he Regulations on the subject as well as terms and conditions of the contract. He wi ll be liable for the deduction of TDS @ 2% on the total bill as Income Tax as per pro vision of the Income Tax Act, or as applicable from time to time. Apart from this, th e Contractor shall also pay GST as per rule fixed by the Govt from time to time. The Contractor will wholly responsible to pay GST. 57. Any obligation and/or formalities which are required to be fulfilled under the Cont ract Labour (Regulation & Abolition) Act, 1970 as amended from time to time or an y other Act for the purpose of entering into and/or execution of this contract shall b e carried out by the Contractor at his own expenses, etc., and the Contractor shall r eport the compliance thereof to the Sr.DSC/RPF/SBP. The Contractor shall be solely liable for violation of any provisions of the said Act or any other Act. 58. The Contractor shall take all reasonable precautions to prevent any unlawful act or disorderly conduct of his employees so deployed for the preservation of peace a nd protection of persons and property of Rly. 59. In case any of the persons so deployed by the Contractor does not come up to th e mark or does not perform his duties satisfactorily or indulges in any unlawful act o r misconduct, the contractor shall take suitable action against such employee on th e direction of the Sr. DSC/RPF/SBP or any other officer so authorized by him in this r egard. 60. In case of any complain/defect pointed out by the authorities, the Contractor shal l immediately replace the person so deployed. 61. LEAVE: - The Contractor shall deploy his employees in such a way that they get weekly rest and other holidays, if admissible under various laws, which may be app licable in this regard. Leave Reserve in the ratio of 1:6 for weekly rest and other hol idays will be provided excluding from the sanctioned strength. 62. It is obligatory on Contractor to comply with all provisions/ rules/ regulations und er various acts and applicable as per Central Govt. Minimum Wages Act. 63. Railway will not be responsible for any violation/contravention of the aforesaid laws , rules and regulations. 64. Contractor will apply to the Labour Commissioner for obtaining a labour License and will submit a copy of license to Administration Section within 30 days from the date of award of contract. 65. The Contractor shall not appoint any Sub-Company/Agency to carry out any oblig ation under the contract. 66. The Contractor shall provide the details of the staff, proposed to be deployed viz. , their name, father’s name, DOB, residential address, Telephone number, recent p assport size photograph in the form of a data base in both hard & soft form and als o provide a local police clearance certificate. Police verification is mandatory in r espect of all staff employed. The same shall be submitted to Sr.DSC/RPF/Office/SBP . 67. No employee of the Contractor shall work for more than 26/27 man days in a mo nth or as specified by Labour Laws. Weekly off is mandatory for all as per labour la ws.

68. The Contractor shall have proper standard and procedures of recruitment and tr aining. The Contractor will provide a copy of Training Manual for inspection of Rly A dministration. 69. The Contractor shall have a proper system for checking on duty security guards, day & night for every shift. Records of the same should be effectively maintained fo r periodically checking of Rly Administration. 70. The service provider will also ensure that workers deployed in this Department ar e medically fit and keep record of their medical fitness at regular intervals. The co mpany shall withdraw such workers and supervisors, who are not found suitable by the Railway for any reasons. The copies of medical fitness certificate of the workers , who are to be deployed in this Department, shall be submitted by the successful t enderer to Sr. DSC/RPF/SBP. 71. The service provider shall appoint a coordinator, who would be responsible for i mmediate interaction with the Department and the Tenderer, so that optimal servic es are available without disruption. 72. The tenderer shall be directly responsible for settlement of any dispute or grievance of the workers relating to their deployment in E.Co.Railway a nd any other matters that may arise. Railway, in no way, shall be responsi ble for settlement of such issues/disputes. 73. Any liability regarding payments of wages to the workers arising due to any hum an loss/injury during the course of work will be the sole and personal responsibility of the Tenderer. 74. The successful service provider/contractor shall submit an undertaking with a for m of affidavit of appropriate value in connection with payment of security guards a s per minimum wages act(Central) and proper contribution towards EPF & ESI of th e employees and Employer every month. 75. The contract will be for a maximum period of two years, which may vary dependi ng upon performance of the tenderer and the requirement of the Department. 76. If, the service provider is found unsatisfactory in any manner, the Rly h ave full power to discontinue the services by giving 7 days prior notice to the contractor. The decision of the Railway Administration in this regard s hall be final. 77. The workers shall not be entitled for any financial benefits/emoluments that are admissible to regular employees of Railways. However, the service provider is requi red to pay wages to the workers engaged strictly as per the Minimum Wages Act m odified from time to time including EPF, ESI and other social security schemes of th e Ministry of Labour. The weekly rest etc. should also be allowed to workers as per statutory provisions. All the statutory requirement such as obtaining valid Labour Li cense on the basis of LOA and compliance of all the provisions of social security legi slations in general and provisions of the Contract Labour (Regulation & Abolition) A ct, 1971 and the Contract Labour (R&A) Rules,1972 are required to be complied wit h by the Tenderer 78. The service provider will ensure to make payment of wages to the security guard s by 7th of every month. 79. The service provider must be registered under Contract Labour Act and must ha ve the valid labour license for at least 150 workers from the competent Licensing of ficer under the provisions of the Contract Labour (regulation & Abolition) Act.

80. The payment of wages to the workers have to be made by the tenderer in accord ance with the provision of Section 21 of the service provider labour (Regulation & A bolition) Act, 1970. The provisions of the said section are given as under: “(Section:21) Responsibility for the payment of wages : (1) A service provider shall be responsible for payment of wages to each worker em ployed by him as contract labour and such wages shall be paid before the expiry of such period as may be prescribed. (2) Every principal employer shall nominate a representative duly authorized by him to be present at the time of disbursement of wages by the service provider and it shall duty of such representative to certify the amounts paid as wages in such manner as may be prescribed. (3) It shall be the duty of the service provider to ensure the disbursement of wages i n the presence of the authorized representative of the principal employer. (4) In case the service provider fails to make payment of wages within the prescribed period or makes short payment, then the principal employer shall be liable to make payment of wages in full or the unpaid balance due, as the case may be, to the con tract labour employed by the service provider and recover the amount so paid from the service provider either by deduction from any amount payable to the service pr ovider under any contract of as a debt payable by the service provider”. 81. Railway authority may exercise power to increase/decrease the requirement of security guards by giving prior notice to the contractor. 82. Railway authority will empower to cancel/reject/modify of the tender, whenever r ailway authority required. 83. Service & Support: An Office of the Service Provider must be located i n the State of Consignee. Documentary evidence to be submitted otherwi se the tender can’t be accepted.
